Point the camera at the phrase instead of typing it.

## ✨ Added

- **Scan the connection phrase.** The web UI has shown a QR code beside the phrase since the phrase existed, and nothing could read it: the scanner in this app was wired only to the old direct-address screen. It is on the phrase screen now, so joining a group is aiming the camera at the other machine rather than typing twelve words on a phone keyboard - which is exactly the input a phone keyboard is worst at.
- **A scanned phrase joins straight away.** The code carries the same twelve words the Connect button would be pressed with, so there is no extra tap after the scan. Typing still works unchanged, for when the other machine's screen is not in front of you.
- **A wrong code says so.** Scanning something that is not a phrase is caught by the same checksum a typo hits, and names what is wrong, rather than dialling a group nobody is in.

## 📋 Notes

- **`versionCode` is 5.** It goes up on every build handed to anybody - it is what Android decides upgrade order by, and two builds sharing one are indistinguishable to a phone.
- **No new permission.** Camera access was already configured for the address scanner on the other screen; this reuses it.
- **Still the encrypted protocol from 1.2.0**, so the instances in the group have to be on a matching build. An instance running an older server will ignore what this app sends.
- **The QR is the phrase**, which is worth knowing before showing that screen to a room or a camera: whoever reads the code holds the whole group, exactly as if they had read the words out loud.
